title: In UN speech, Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal reached
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened Tuesday to “annihilate” Iran if diplomatic efforts to end his nearly seven-month-old war do not succeed. Speaking to the United Nations General Assembly, he also touted both his peacemaking record and an increasingly belligerent U.S. foreign policy stretching from the Middle East to Venezuela to Greenland. Trump presented the past year as proof that military force and economic pressure could resolve conflicts that diplomacy had failed to settle. “As president of the most extraordinary nation in history, I have no interest in leaving dangers to grow for another day,” he declared. “I do not believe in letting problems fester; they only become harder to solve. title: China is outfoxing the US in the battle for Mideast influence
summary: Washington talks about “influence” as though it were a mystical vapor that leaks out of every military base closure. But Beijing’s rapidly growing clout in the Middle East shows that influence can come in many forms. While the Pentagon debates whether and where to rebuild U.S. bases battered by Iran during Operation Epic Fury, China has spent the last decade expanding its influence in the Middle East without stationing a single soldier there. China’s experience in the region makes clear that influence can be cultivated far more cheaply than Washington assumes, and without maintaining a sprawling network of vulnerable military installations. As Operation Epic Fury demonstrated, Washington’s constellation of fixed bases across the Middle East is vulnerable and expensive to defend. Before the war, the United States maintained at least 19 military facilities across the region, eight of them considered permanent. Iranian attacks left both the headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet in Bahrain and the Qatar command center , from which the United States had coordinated regional air operations for more than two decades, effectively inoperable. title: Trump and Xi meet on a 'rotting' diplomatic foundation
summary: As Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his third meeting in less than a year with U.S. President Donald Trump, calm seems to prevail in the relationship. This is a dangerous illusion. The sense of stability is breeding complacency on both sides even as pressure builds up under the surface. We may be throwing away our last opening to put the world’s most important bilateral relationship on a solid foundation. In keeping with the slogan on which the two sides agreed at their May meeting in Beijing, the U.S. and China are supposedly building a relationship of “constructive strategic stability.” Indeed, compared to the confrontational posture of both sides during the first Trump and Biden administrations, we seem to have stepped back from the brink of conflict. Even the seemingly explosive issue of the ongoing U.S. assault against Iran and its damaging consequences for the global economy, or China’s continued dealings with Iran that are frustrating the U.S. strategy of economic strangulation, do not seem to be major grievances for either side. title: When Saudi Arabia realizes it's backed the wrong horse
summary: The United States went to war with Iran in the belief that American power could quickly overwhelm Tehran’s ability to threaten the Middle East. For Saudi Arabia, the war is producing nearly the opposite result. Iran has been badly hit, but it and its regional allies have demonstrated that they can still threaten Saudi cities, oil installations, pipelines and export routes. At the same time, Washington has shown that even overwhelming offensive power does not necessarily translate into effective protection for its Gulf partners. The consequence is likely to be a historic Saudi reassessment: less confidence in the United States, more reliance on regional partners and a much closer strategic relationship with China. Saudi Arabia’s geographical problem is not new. In an article published in LobeLog in September 2019 , I described the “encirclement” of Saudi oil production by Iran and Iran-aligned forces. That year, the attack on the Abqaiq processing complex displayed the accuracy and reach of the weapons available to Tehran or its allies . title: Police hugging AI so tight, soon we'll all be pre-crime suspects
summary: Earlier this month, an announcement by an Anthropic researcher that so-called “Superintelligent AI” has a greater than 10% chance of destroying humanity over the next decade triggered widespread alarm. “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans,” wrote Evan Hubinger, Anthropic’s Alignment Science Lead. Those risks are, of course, real and terrifying. But perhaps of more immediate concern are the ways in which humans are already using AI, not how AI will potentially escape human control. Though it has been mostly ignored by corporate media, the U.S. security state is now seeking out and collaborating with AI firms on “offensive cyber ops”; AI targeting systems; and efforts to sift through and interpret vast troves of data on American citizens and foreigners collected by the U.S. government. title: Why Trump won't 'blow the sh*t out of' Oman today
summary: The Sultanate of Oman’s willingness to engage all actors in the Middle East and beyond has long been a pillar of Muscat’s foreign policy. Yet with the war raging in the region, Oman’s efforts to maintain a pragmatic and normal relationship with Iran has fueled friction with the White House. This was notably underscored by President Donald J. Trump’s earlier threats to “ blow up ” and “ bomb the shit out of ” Oman in response to Muscat’s talks with Tehran about the future status of the Strait of Hormuz. Despite these threats, it is clear that Washington recognizes Oman’s value as a bridge to Iran and other regional actors. With the struggle for control over Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandab becoming the “ Western Front ” in the wider U.S.-Iran crisis, the Trump administration has turned to Oman for help with de-escalation efforts and direct talks between Washington and the Ansar Allah movement, better known as the Houthis.
